```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# Reads the example code from inst/examples, so that the vignette always
# shows the same examples as the help pages
exempel <- function(fn) {
  fil <- file.path("..", "inst", "examples", paste0(fn, ".R"))
  if (!file.exists(fil)) fil <- system.file("examples", paste0(fn, ".R"), package = "pxweb2rgui")
  readLines(fil, encoding = "UTF-8")
}
```

The package fetches statistics from sites that publish data through PxWeb API
v1 or v2, by default Statistics Sweden (SCB). It finds tables, lists the values of
their variables, builds the query and returns a tidy tibble. Large requests
are split into several calls within the API's limits, labels can be used
instead of codes, `"9999"` means the latest period, and DeSO and RegSO areas
are split by municipality.

This vignette follows a typical workflow: find a table, look at the values of
its variables, and fetch the data. All examples need internet access, so the
vignette shows the code without running it. Run it in your own session; every
call fetches only a little data.

```{r}
library(pxweb2rgui)
```

## Providers and languages

Every function takes the statistics provider, as `provider` or, in
`pxr_pxweb2_get_data()`, as `base_url`. It can be `"scb"` (Statistics
Sweden), `"ssb"` (Statistics Norway), `"dst"` (Statistics Denmark), one of the
providers with PxWeb API v1
below, or the address of any PxWeb API v1 or v2. The
addresses of the providers are stored in the package. Without `lang` the
provider's default language is used, or `getOption("pxweb2r.lang")` if you
have set it.

`provider` is `"scb"` by default. To leave it out, name the other arguments, as
in `pxr_get_all_codes(tab = "TAB638")`. The names can be written in upper or lower
case:

| Name | Statistics agency | API |
|---|---|---|
| `"scb"` | Statistics Sweden | v2 |
| `"ssb"` | Statistics Norway | v2 |
| `"dst"` | Statistics Denmark | its own |
| `"statfin"` | Statistics Finland | v1 |
| `"fohm"` | Public Health Agency of Sweden | v1 |
| `"sjv"` | Swedish Board of Agriculture | v1 |
| `"tillvaxtanalys"` | Swedish Agency for Growth Policy Analysis | v1 |
| `"konj"` | National Institute of Economic Research, Sweden | v1 |
| `"skolverket"` | Swedish National Agency for Education | v1 |
| `"vgr_arbetsmarknad"` | Region Västra Götaland: labour market and business | v1 |
| `"vgr_demografi"` | Region Västra Götaland: demography | v1 |
| `"vgr_folkhalsa"` | Region Västra Götaland: public health survey | v1 |
| `"vgr_gransregional"` | Region Västra Götaland: cross-border statistics Norway-Sweden | v1 |
| `"vgr_personal"` | Region Västra Götaland: staff statistics | v1 |
| `"nordicstats"` | Nordic Statistics (Nordregio), all the Nordic countries | v1 |

## PxWeb API v1

Every function also works with sites that have PxWeb API v1. The built-in
providers are `"statfin"` (Statistics Finland), `"fohm"`
(Public Health Agency of Sweden), `"sjv"` (Swedish Board of Agriculture),
`"tillvaxtanalys"` (Growth Analysis), `"konj"` (National Institute of Economic
Research), `"skolverket"` (National Agency for Education) and the five databases
of Region Västra Götaland, whose names start with `"vgr_"`, and `"nordicstats"`
(Nordic Statistics from Nordregio, in English only). For other sites,
give the address with its language and database. An address with `/v1/` (or
`/v0/`) in it is API v1.

A provider that has both API v1 and v2 is always used through v2, also if you
give the address of its v1, and a message says so. That applies to Statistics
Sweden and Statistics Norway. Give the language with `lang`, since the language in
the v1 address is then not used. For other sites the package checks once per
session whether v2 exists, so a provider that moves to v2 is followed
automatically. Tables have other ids in v2, so a path from v1 gives an error that
explains this; find the new id with `pxr_search_tabs()`.

In API v1 the table id is the table's path, as `pxr_get_all_tabs()` gives it in
the column `tabellid`, for example
`"Animalieproduktion/Mejeriproduktion/JO0604A1.px"`. An id without folders, such
as `"JO0604A1"`, with or without `.px` and in upper or lower case, also works: the
package finds the table's path in the table list before it asks the site. If tables
in several folders have that name, such as `"EDUC11"` in Nordic Statistics, you get
an error that lists their paths, since tables with the same name can have different
contents. The first such id in a session reads the table list, see below. Apart
from that the calls look the same, but some things differ because the API lacks
them:

- `pxr_get_all_tabs()` and `pxr_search_tabs()`: there is no list of tables. The
  site's search is used to build it, and where there is none every folder is
  read. On a large site that can take some minutes the first time in a
  session, and a message says so when it starts.
- `pxr_pxweb2_get_data()`: there are no code lists. `include_aggregations` gives
  a warning and is ignored, and the column `kommun` is empty for DeSO areas, also
  with a warning. `kommun_kod` is complete, and RegSO areas get both.
- `pxweb2_gui()` and `pxweb2_gui_addin()`: "Välj indelning" is not there,
  discontinued tables cannot be told apart and the table list shows no periods.
  The interface says so when such a site is chosen.
- There is no list of languages. For a site outside the package's list of
  providers the interface offers only the language in the address, and `lang`
  in the functions is tried against the site.

## Statistics Denmark

Statistics Denmark has an API of its own, which is not PxWeb, but the functions
are used in the same way with the provider `"dst"`. The languages are `"da"`
(default) and `"en"`. The API has no code lists, so `include_aggregations` gives a
warning and is ignored, and "Välj indelning" is not in the interface. The result
always has a column with the table's content named `Indhold`, also with
`lang = "en"`. Large requests are split as usual, and discontinued tables and
periods work in the table list.

## Find a table

`pxr_get_all_tabs()` lists every table of a provider as a data frame with the
columns `tabellid`, `tab_name` and `updated`. `pxr_search_tabs()` keeps the
tables whose names contain any of the texts in `search_str`, without regard to
upper or lower case. Both take `updated_since`, a date such as `"2026-05-12"`,
to keep only tables updated on or after that day.

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_get_all_tabs"), eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_search_tabs"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Labels and codes of the variables

`pxr_get_labels()` and `pxr_get_codes()` give the labels or codes of one
variable, filtered by text (required: `tab`, `var`).
`pxr_get_all_labels()` and `pxr_get_all_codes()` give every value of a table,
per variable (required: `tab`).

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_get_labels"), eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_get_codes"), eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_get_all_labels"), eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_get_all_codes"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Comments on a table

Providers often write comments that are needed to read the figures right, such as
changes in a regional division. `pxr_get_comments()` (required: `tab`) gives them as
a `tibble` with one row per comment. The column `niva` tells whether a comment is on
the whole table, a variable or a value, and `obligatorisk` whether the provider says
it must be shown with the figures. API v2 has the comments in the metadata. PxWeb API
v1 sends them only with data, so there the function makes one small data request per
variable and one more. Statistics Denmark has comments on the whole table only.

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_get_comments"), eval = FALSE}
```

### Using the labels and codes together

A common task is to pick values by their names and then fetch data with the
codes. Here the municipalities in Dalarna whose names end with "a" are chosen,
and their population is fetched for the last two years.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
kommuner <- pxr_get_codes("scb", "TAB638", "Region", starts_with = "20",
                          n_chars = 4)
namn <- pxr_get_codes("scb", "TAB638", "Region", starts_with = "20",
                      n_chars = 4, to_labels = TRUE)
valda <- kommuner[endsWith(tolower(namn), "a")]

ar <- tail(pxr_get_all_codes("scb", "TAB638")$Tid, 2)

pxr_pxweb2_get_data("TAB638", query = list(
  Region = valda, Civilstand = NA, Alder = "tot", Kon = NA,
  ContentsCode = "BE0101N1", Tid = ar))
```

The filters can also be used to check a table before you fetch from it, for
example whether a region is there and what it is called.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pxr_get_labels("scb", "TAB638", "Region", contains = "göteborg")
pxr_get_codes("scb", "TAB638", "Region", starts_with = "1480", to_labels = TRUE)
```

## Fetch data

`pxr_pxweb2_get_data()` is the main function. `table` is required: a table id
or a vector of table ids. `query` is a named list with one element per
variable; variables left out get all their values, and `NA` eliminates a
variable. Codes and labels both work as values, and `"*"`, `"9999"` (latest
period), `top(n)`, `from()`, `to()` and `range()` are understood. By default
only labels are returned; `code_variables` adds a code column,
`<variable>_kod`, for the variables you name.

```{r, code = exempel("pxr_pxweb2_get_data"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Several tables

Give `table` a vector of ids and each table is called with the variables and
values that exist in it. If `Tid = c("2023", "2024", "2025")` is asked for, and
one table has 2023 and 2024 and another has 2025, the first is called with 2023
and 2024 and the second with 2025. A table with none of the values asked for in a
variable it can eliminate is called without the variable, so its rows cover all
values of that variable. A table is not called if it lacks the values of a variable
it requires, if such a variable is `NA`, or if it lacks the values of a region.
`"9999"` is each table's own latest period. Messages say what was done. The results
are combined with
`dplyr::bind_rows()`, and the first column, `table_id`, says where a row comes
from. Columns that only some tables have are `NA` in the rows of the other tables,
and a warning says which.

`pxr_get_labels()`, `pxr_get_codes()`, `pxr_get_all_labels()` and
`pxr_get_all_codes()` also take several ids in `tab` and combine the values without
duplicates. Tables that lack the variable are passed over, and it is an error
only if no table has it. In the graphical interface, Ctrl+click selects several
tables.

## The graphical interface

`pxweb2_gui()` opens an interface where you choose provider, language, table,
variables and values, and get ready-made `pxr_pxweb2_get_data()` code. In
RStudio it is also an addin, `pxweb2_gui_addin()`. See
`vignette("pxweb2rgui", package = "pxweb2rgui")`.

## Overview of the functions

| Function | What it does | Required arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `pxr_get_all_tabs()` | All tables of a provider, with update dates | – |
| `pxr_search_tabs()` | Tables whose names contain a text | `search_str` |
| `pxr_get_labels()` | Labels of a variable, filtered by text | `tab`, `var` |
| `pxr_get_codes()` | Codes of a variable, filtered by text | `tab`, `var` |
| `pxr_get_all_labels()` | All labels of a table, per variable | `tab` |
| `pxr_get_all_codes()` | All codes of a table, per variable | `tab` |
| `pxr_get_comments()` | Comments on a table, its variables and values | `tab` |
| `pxr_pxweb2_get_data()` | Fetch data | `table` |
| `pxweb2_gui()` | Open the graphical interface | – |
| `pxweb2_gui_addin()` | RStudio addin: statistics table to code | – |
